# Business Buzz: United States’ September job and employment report

 In News
 October 12, 2026
 Beckett Showalter

Business Buzz: United States’ September job and employment report

The United States labor market reported that the economy added 29,000 jobs and the unemployment rate increased to 4.2% in the month of September. With the midterm elections happening in November, what does this data mean for Republicans? [...] Specific data shows that there was very little change in specific demographics from August to September. The unemployment rates for adult men, women and teenagers showed little change over the month. The jobless rate for White, Asian and Hispanic people also showed little change. However, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported that the unemployment rate for African Americans increased in the month of September to 7%, a 1% increase from August.

# US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week

By Thomson Reuters Oct 8, 2026 | 8:36 AM

By Lucia Mutikani

WASHINGTON, Oct 8 (Reuters) – The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to continued labor market stability despite a sharp slowdown in job growth in September. [...] “An ongoing rise in unemployment among new entrants and re-entrants to the labor market, amid weak hiring, will put some further gentle upward pressure on the unemployment rate over the next few quarters,” said Samuel Tombs, chief US economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

(Reporting by ​Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Paul Simao)

results.content: Nonfarm payrolls increased ​by 29,000 jobs last month after a downwardly revised rise of 133,000 in August, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls would advance by 90,000 after ⁠a previously reported surge of 162,000 in August. Estimates ranged from as low as 35,000 to as high as 180,000. [...] "This is a disappointing jobs report and a reminder that the low-hire, low-fire labor market never went away," said ​Olu Sonola, head of US economics at Fitch Ratings. "Weak job growth, a slightly higher unemployment rate, contained wage gains and downward revisions to earlier payroll estimates give the Fed little reason to keep an October rate hike on the table." results.title: September Jobs Gain Falls Short at 29,000 as Rate Hits 4.2%
results.content:
### Why It Matters

RealPage economist Chuck Ehmann describes the labor market as resilient but sluggish. The headline unemployment rate rose slightly to 4.2% and has stayed between 4.1% and 4.3% since March.

Job growth feeds office, retail and apartment demand, so a weak monthly print and downward revisions give CRE investors and operators less cushion to lean on.

### What's Next [...] ### Key Takeaways

 The U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs in September on a seasonally adjusted basis, well short of economists' expectations, and July and August were revised down by 60,000 combined.
 Education and health services led gains at 20,000 jobs, while government lost 17,000 jobs, mostly in local government outside education.
 Unemployment edged up to 4.2%, staying inside the 4.1% to 4.3% range it has held since March, which RealPage's economist describes as resilient but sluggish. [...] ### What's Next

The next Bureau of Labor Statistics report will show whether September's weakness was a one-off or the start of a longer slowdown, and whether revisions keep running lower.
